advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix scenarios 6 and 8 to expect the exception `bridge_sync` actually raises (RebarError) — or match the guard message — since `run_pass_result` converts CrossProjectTargetError into an OPERATIONAL_FAILURE/RebarError before it reaches the caller.
evidence: test file: `with pytest.raises(CrossProjectTargetError):\n        rebar.bridge_sync(repo_root=str(work))` at test_multi_project_rehearsal.py:538 and :614
src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:195-212 — `_bridge_run` calls `orchestrator.run_pass_result(...)` then `if returncode: ... raise RebarError(message, returncode=returncode, ...)`
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:505-520 — `try: result = reconcile.reconcile_once(...) except Exception as exc: return _reconcile_exception_result(exc, ...)` catches the guard error
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py:628-638 — `CrossProjectTargetError` is raised inside the applier, i.e. within the `reconcile_once` call that run_pass_result guards
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_cross_project_guard.py:129 — the only tests that catch CrossProjectTargetError do so by calling the applier directly, not via bridge_sync
advisory.finding: Scenarios 6 and 8 assert `pytest.raises(CrossProjectTargetError)` around `rebar.bridge_sync(...)`, but the library never surfaces that exception type: `_bridge_run` calls `run_pass_result`, which wraps `reconcile_once` in `except Exception` and classifies the guard's `CrossProjectTargetError` as `OPERATIONAL_FAILURE` (canonical_exit=1); `_bridge_run` then raises `RebarError`, not `CrossProjectTargetError`. Both scenarios will fail with the wrong-exception-type mismatch when run live.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `pytest.raises(CrossProjectTargetError)` with `pytest.raises(rebar.RebarError)` (optionally asserting the message mentions 'outside the configured scope'), matching how the library surfaces the guard through bridge_sync.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen scenario 1 to assert the two ingested local tickets map to the two seeded projects (e.g. read back each seeded issue's local binding), not merely mutations_applied>=2.
evidence: `assert applied >= 2, f"inbound sync applied only {applied} mutations for two seeded issues"`

Comment concedes: "A LIVE sync carries no plan in its details, so assert the observable apply outcome" — but the assertion is a count, not a per-project/per-ticket content check unlike the outbound scenarios which query by label per project.
advisory.finding: Scenario 1 (test_inbound_from_both_projects) verifies the applied inbound only via a bare `mutations_applied >= 2` count; it does not assert that the two ingested tickets correspond to the two seeded projects. The headline routing invariant is pinned in preview, but the observable apply outcome cannot detect a regression where inbound mis-routes/mis-attributes yet still totals >=2 mutations.
scenarios: An inbound regression that ingests two tickets but attributes both to the wrong project (or ingests unrelated tickets) still yields applied>=2 and passes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin scenarios 7 and 10 to the concrete expected exception type (or match= on the message) instead of a bare pytest.raises(Exception).
evidence: `with pytest.raises(Exception):  # noqa: B017 — backend/transport error type is not pinned`
Scenario 7 raises Exception for BOTH bridge_preview and bridge_sync; scenario 10 uses `with pytest.raises(Exception): dc_transport.get_issue(probe)` for the delete-confirmation 404.
The `after == before` (scenario 7) and injected-flag (scenario 10) companions constrain side effects but not the exception's cause.
advisory.finding: Scenarios 7 (unknown-project fail-closed) and 10 (cleanup 404) assert `pytest.raises(Exception)` with a fully-unpinned base type. A bug that raises for an unrelated reason (e.g. a config/import error before the fail-closed path executes) would satisfy the raise and pass, weakening the fail-closed / delete-confirmation contract these scenarios are meant to prove.
scenarios: A regression where the pass aborts early for the wrong reason still raises SOME Exception and passes the fail-closed assertion.
